title: USB serial enumeration can exceed caller capacity on multi-interface devices
evidence: indigo_usbserial_utils.c:100-111: macOS outer USB loop checks count < num_serial_info, but inner descendant loop writes serial_info[count] and increments for every serial endpoint without checking capacity. A multi-interface device when one slot remains overwrites caller storage. Framework indigo_driver.c:280 supplies a fixed MAX_DEVICE_PORTS array.

title: Explicit-port URL parsers do not bound the copied hostname
evidence: indigo_uni_io.c:1584-1588 and indigo_io.c:367-370: explicit-port URL parsing copies colon-host bytes to host_name[INDIGO_NAME_SIZE] and writes a terminator at the same unbounded index. Public helpers accept longer URLs; drivers pass device URL property strings into this path. A malformed/overlong hostname corrupts stack before any network connection.

title: HID close falls through into descriptor cleanup
evidence: indigo_uni_io.c:2389-2409: POSIX HID close calls hid_close(copy->hid_device), then continues through socket operations and close(copy->fd). indigo_uni_handle declares fd/hid_device in the same union, so these operations use pointer bits as a descriptor. Usually EBADF; a matching descriptor can be closed spuriously. Current wheel_atik/wheel_sx open via indigo_uni_open_hid.

Correction to early reviewer message: the aliased fd is not necessarily zero; the public union layout disproves that early detail.

title: RAW-to-FITS conversion lacks input and header capacity checks
evidence: indigo_fits.c:69-119, 140-179: converter reads RAW header before checking in_size, computes signed size products without validating dimensions/payload, and emits unbounded sprintf keyword cards into one fixed 2880-byte header. Embedded extension cards have no remaining-header check. Short/corrupt RAW input or large metadata can read/write beyond allocations; many cards also overwrite the data region. Called by the file converter at indigo_tools/indigo_raw_to_fits.c:185.

title: RAW selection geometry permits inclusive reads outside the frame
evidence: indigo_raw_utils.c:438-449 and 667-675: selection guards accept xx == width-radius or yy == height-radius, but inclusive loops reach index width/height. PSF accesses all formats directly; selection digest RGB/RGBA variants do too. Public APIs and imager star selection can reach frame-edge selections. Radius zero also allocates zero border storage in PSF before writing one border value. PSF lines 509-515 use int squared-deviation sum, which overflows for ordinary high-contrast 16-bit borders and corrupts HFD/FWHM thresholds.

title: Small-frame Bayer equalization mixes sampling parities

title: Cartesian conversion maps negative coordinate axes incorrectly

title: Device-reported filter counts exceed allocated property arrays
evidence: driver-b-review.md section B-01; exact current source paths and contract evidence in that section.
summary: `wheel_trutek/indigo_wheel_trutek.driver:49`, `wheel_xagyl/indigo_wheel_xagyl.driver:58`, and `wheel_qhy/indigo_wheel_qhy.driver:106` assign response-derived `WHEEL_SLOT_NAME_PROPERTY->count` and `WHEEL_SLOT_OFFSET_PROPERTY->count` without checking the allocated capacities. Base wheel attach in `indigo_libs/indigo_wheel_driver.c:53` allocates16 slots. Trutek byte0xFF decodes207, Xagyl `FilterSlots 100` decodes100 and QHY `MXP` reply `Z` decodes35. Those become authoritative property counts; consumers iterate count rather than magically resizing the allocation. Corrupt/device-invalid responses can therefore expose invalid property metadata and out-of-bounds item access. `driver-b-evidence/wheel-count-contract.json` retains literal-expression examples; no malformed frame was sent to a real driver/device. Remediation: validate reply framing/checksum where applicable and the count against both `allocated_count` fields before storing or publishing; reject connection/readback on invalid counts. Add malformed-count simulator regressions proving no property publication exceeds allocation. Do not merely clamp device facts or weaken framework/client validation.

title: Motion completion lacks an overall timeout in several wheels/mounts
evidence: driver-b-review.md section B-02; exact current source paths and contract evidence in that section.
summary: `wheel_quantum/indigo_wheel_quantum.driver:36-40` repeatedly reads valid `P` positions until the requested slot; a controller continuing to report another slot never lets this synchronous handler return. Individual serial read timeout does not bound a stream of valid replies, so disconnect is queued behind it. Related asynchronous endless-BUSY shapes occur in `wheel_trutek:77-80` (slot0), `wheel_xagyl:99-102` (wrong slot), `wheel_asi:155-156` and calibration175-176 (`pos == -1`), `wheel_playerone:149-155` (the30-poll bound applies only to initial target0, not ordinary motion), `mount_pmc8:620-622` (moving park rates), and `mount_temma:297-301` (GOTO status s1; park already has a deadline). Remediation: use monotonic operation deadlines and bounded finalizers, retain last measured position and requested target, publish ALERT on expiry, and perform protocol-supported stop/recovery. Characterize stationary/wrong-target/endless-moving replies plus queued abort/disconnect. Bounded transport transactions alone are not whole-operation timeouts.

title: Lakeside valid stationary progress replies evade the stall bound
evidence: driver-b-review.md section B-03; exact current source paths and contract evidence in that section.
summary: `focuser_lakeside/indigo_focuser_lakeside.driver:177-225`: failed reads and unexpected lines increment `stalled`, but a valid repeated `P<n>` enters218-225, resets only if position changed, and otherwise reschedules without incrementing. An endless repeated position without DONE never reaches40, contradicting the comment's claimed stall bound. The handler yields, but the client remains BUSY and further motion stays excluded indefinitely. Remediation: count unchanged valid position frames or impose a separate overall deadline, send existing CH stop on expiry, preserve target and publish ALERT. Regression: repeated stationary P frames without DONE; genuine progressing P followed by DONE must still succeed.

title: SynScan AUTOHOME blocks its own queued abort/disconnect
evidence: driver-b-review.md section B-04; exact current source paths and contract evidence in that section.
summary: `mount_synscan/indigo_mount_synscan.driver:2132` calls `synscan_perform_autohome()` synchronously from AUTOHOME on_change. The helper calls30-second stopped-axis loops577-595,120-second index loops644-665 and711-764, and a three-second sleep698. The loops inspect `abort_motion`, but this source sets the flag only in the queued abort handler1961 and disconnect hook1672. There is no bus-thread on_change_request setting it. These handlers share the serialized queue and cannot run while auto-home waits. Urgent priority cannot preempt the currently executing callback. A requested abort/disconnect can consequently wait through multi-stage physical homing. Remediation: staged handler/finalizer home state machine with bounded single-transaction checks and named cancellation/stop paths. Preserve documented device command order; add timed simulator assertions that abort/disconnect execute during each stage, verify actual stop-command edges and failure/timeout state, then perform authorized hardware validation in the repair task. Merely setting a volatile flag is not a substitute for queue ownership/cancellation and does not resolve the synchronous waits.

title: Stopped-short moves are reported successful
evidence: driver-b-review.md section B-05; exact current source paths and contract evidence in that section.
summary: Several authored finalizers treat idle as arrival despite having measured position and retaining a different requested target: `focuser_mypro2/indigo_focuser_mypro2.driver:333-338`, `focuser_dsd:215-217`, `focuser_dmfc:277-278`, `focuser_fc3:223-224`, `focuser_asi:207-208`, `focuser_usbv3:254-255`, and shared Lunatico rotator `focuser_lunatico/shared/lunatico_shared.c:889`. For example, mypro2 target1000, measured500 and moving0 enters the unconditional OK branch; the caller cannot distinguish target arrival from premature device stop. Shared Lunatico affects the rotator interface exposed by both focuser_lunatico and rotator_lunatico. Alpaca absolute focuser is excluded from this finding: its canonical class contract in `system_alpaca/indigo_system_alpaca_private.h` explicitly defines completion by IsMoving rather than comparing positions. Its deliberate settling window and idle completion are consistent with that accepted contract. A proposed target-equality finding there is rejected; changing the contract requires a separate explicit product decision. Remediation: distinguish commanded vs external/aborted motion, compare measured position with commanded expected position using protocol-appropriate tolerance/backlash semantics, publish ALERT on stopped-short and retain requested target. Add one early-stop regression per affected driver rather than assuming all protocols are identical. Existing exact-target handling in Astroasis, FLI, EFA, FocusDreamPro, Askar and SteelDrive2 shows a local behavior-preserving pattern.

title: Falcon direction setter accepts failed/mismatched acknowledgements
evidence: driver-b-review.md section B-06; exact current source paths and contract evidence in that section.
summary: `rotator_falcon/indigo_rotator_falcon.driver:222` tests `!falcon_command(...) && !strncmp(response, "FN:", 3)`. A transport-successful reply `ERR` makes the first operand false and never sets ALERT. A failed command with a different/empty reply also makes the prefix operand false. The generated prologue therefore publishes the requested reversal OK even when its acknowledgement is invalid or absent. `driver-b-evidence/falcon-direction-truth-table.json` records the exact Boolean truth table, not a hardware test. Remediation: require transport success AND valid acknowledgement (failure OR invalid prefix), preserve/read back prior direction on failure, and regress success/refusal/timeout/stale reply combinations. Keep changes in the .driver and regenerate without changing generator semantics.

title: Native registries fail to reject their exact capacity boundary

title: Partial SESSION_FEATURES update copies another client's setting
evidence: core-functional-review.md section C-02; exact source and ordinary functional proof retained there.
summary: `indigo_libs/indigo_session.c:51-67` stores feature values in one shared property. Enumeration writes both fields from the enumerating client, but a change copies only named request items into that shared property and then copies **both** resulting values into the requesting client. For example A has FORCE_ITEM_UPDATES=true; B enumerates with both flags false; A sends only FORCE_PROPERTY_UPDATES=true. A's unmentioned FORCE_ITEM_UPDATES is reset to B's false value. Partial named-item updates are the normal bus contract, and these flags explicitly belong to the requesting client. Remediation: seed the shared response values from the requesting  Full evidence: C-02. Remediation: seed the shared response values from the requesting client under appropriate ownership before applying a partial update, or derive each client field independently from present request items; publish only to that client. Unit regression interleaves two clients' enumeration and one-item updates. No cross-client runtime test was run here.

title: Browser sexagesimal conversion loses the sign below one degree
evidence: core-functional-review.md section C-03; exact source and ordinary functional proof retained there.
summary: `indigo_server/resource/indigo.js:462-490`: dtos truncates signed degrees with `d | 0`, losing the minus sign when -1 < value <0. stod determines the sign using `parseInt(degrees) <0`, which is false for negative zero. Actual Node execution of the committed functions returned `dtos(-0.5) == "0:30:00"` and `stod("-0:30:00") == +0.5`. `components.js:1124-1184` uses these functions for sexagesimal editing/display, and generic property controls use them at1418/1426/1445. `mount.html` uses those controls and dtos for picked target coordinates. Declinations/latitudes just south of zero can therefore be displayed or sent north of zero. Remediation:  Full evidence: C-03. Remediation: preserve the original sign separately from integer degree magnitude in formatting and parse the leading string sign; test positive/negative sub-degree values, zero, nonzero integer degrees and round-trip precision in ordinary coordinate widgets.

title: Browser HOST_TIME emits malformed fractional-hour offsets
evidence: core-functional-review.md section C-04; exact source and ordinary functional proof retained there.
summary: `indigo_server/resource/indigo.js:493-509` divides timezone minutes by60 and concatenates `'00'`, instead of formatting separate whole hours and remainder minutes. With getTimezoneOffset()=-330 the actual committed function produces suffix `+05.500`, whereas an ISO numeric UTC+05:30 offset is `+0530` (or `+05:30`). Every authored page calls timestamp() for initially empty Server.HOST_TIME; server setter `indigo_server.c:1540-1550` forwards the value to its existing date-management helper. Fractional-hour locales can fail first-time host clock setup. Remediation: format signed absolute hours and minutes separately, or use a validated UTC repre Full evidence: C-04. Remediation: format signed absolute hours and minutes separately, or use a validated UTC representation supported by the helper; regress ±30/45-minute offsets and ordinary whole-hour timezones. The test replaced only Date.getTimezoneOffset in an isolated VM; no system clock was changed.

title: Imager deletes original file after an HTTP error response
evidence: core-functional-review.md section C-05; exact source and ordinary functional proof retained there.
summary: `indigo_server/resource/imager.html:507-519` handles xhr.onload by clicking a download link for any response and then sending AGENT_IMAGER_DELETE_FILE with the original filename. onload runs for completed HTTP404/500 responses too, and this callback does not inspect status.
